summary: Xinru Liu specializes in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed a PhD under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985) and held posts at CASS (~1985–2002) and The College of New Jersey (~2002).
Xiuzhi Zeng is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned an MA at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen, attested in 2006.

Xu Dishan (1893–1941) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Yenching, Columbia, and Oxford, and held posts at Tsinghua University (~1926–1935), Peking University (~1926–1935), and the University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).

Xue Yu is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MPhil from the University of Hong Kong (2011–2013). Posts include The Chinese University of Hong Kong, University of Chicago (attested 2026), and Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Xuesong Zhang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, earning a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008). He was attested as associate professor at Renmin University of China in 2015.

Xuezhu Li works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Shoryu Katsura, served as a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University in 2011, and has been a research associate at China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2026).
Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and served as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Yadi Qu is an Indology, Tibetology, and computational scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

Yael Bentor works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington, where Gregory Schopen supervised her doctorate. She has taught Indian Studies and served as professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Yakupitiyage Karunadasa (1934–2026) studied at the University of Ceylon and earned a PhD at the University of London under David Friedman. He served as Director and Emeritus Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and held posts at Kelaniya, HKU, SOAS, Calgary, and Toronto.
Yandong Hou is a Tibetology scholar who studied at and held a post at the Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology.

Yanfei Zhao is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned MAs at Beijing Foreign Studies University and SOAS, continued doctoral studies at BFSU in 2023, and was a visiting PhD student at Yale University (2025–2026).
Yanfei Zhou works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. She earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich by 1998, and also studied under Hojin (attested 2003).
Yangdon Dhondup is a scholar in Tibetology who completed her PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao (~2000–2004).
Yanling Chen specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun (attested 2012).

Yannick Laurent works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He holds posts at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter (attested 2026).
Yanpei (1917–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and was a student of Yinshun around 1941.
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of California by 1997 and held a post as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
